predictions.experiment: Mechanism test: within-cue wrong-answer agreement minus cue-vs-plain wrong-answer agreement on MATH-500 at T 1.0, A - B. The problem-driven-attractor rival predicts about 0.00 (a problem's common wrong value is hit by any base context); this mechanism predicts clearly positive.
predictions.recipe: Files: studies/rlneurons/results/day1_3/math500_base_cue-01/rows.jsonl (CUE) and s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r4/modal_t3-01/t3/T3.jsonl (T3, plain base, T 1.0; fetch with the aws command in inventory.md). CUE: keep rows with attempt == 0; for each (problem_index, sample) keep the first row in file order. A CUE row is a wrong answer iff cap_hit is not true, finish_reason != 'length', score_v3 == 0, and extracted_v3 is a non-empty string after strip(). T3: keep the first row per problem_index in file order; run grader v3 (studies/rlneurons/grader/rln4_grader_v3.py, the procedure that fills score_v3 and extracted_v3) on its text and gold to get its v3 score and v3 extracted answer. A T3 row is a wrong answer iff cap_hit is not true, finish_reason != 'length', v3 score == 0 and the v3 extracted answer is non-empty after strip(). Agreement of two answers = rln4_lib.agree(a, b) from studies/rlneurons/lib/rln4_lib.py (true = agree). A = (number of unordered pairs of CUE wrong answers of the same problem_index that agree) / (number of such pairs), pooled over problems. B = (number of (CUE wrong answer, T3 wrong answer) pairs with the same problem_index that agree) / (number of such pairs), pooled over problems. Statistic = A - B. Problems with fewer than two CUE wrong answers contribute no A pairs; problems without a T3 wrong answer contribute no B pairs. If either denominator is 0 the statistic is undefined and counts as refuted.
predictions.refuted_by: measured A - B below 0.03, or undefined
predictions.note: Files: studies/rlneurons/results/day1_3/math500_base_cue-01/rows.jsonl (CUE, committed) and runs/theory-tests/r4/modal_t3-01/t3/T3.jsonl (fetched with aws s3 cp from s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r4/modal_t3-01/t3/T3.jsonl --profile iterate-ecr; byte-identical to the inventory copy). T3 rows carry no v3 fields, so the script calls rln4_lib.grade_v3(gold, text) (the call rln4_grader_v3.py uses to fill score_v3 / extracted_v3); the hand-review notes JUDGED_INCORRECT in that file are not applied (they do not change the score field). Empty T3 text counts as no extracted answer. Agreement is rln4_lib.agree on the raw extracted_v3 strings (no norm_v3), as written. Ambiguity: agree is asymmetric (its first argument is parsed as gold). Main reading: CUE answer first for B, lower sample index first for A. alt_measured: a pair agrees if agree holds in either order. n = the smaller of the two problem groups (A: problems with >= 2 CUE wrong; B: problems with >= 1 CUE wrong and a T3 wrong). Bootstrap resamples all CUE problems (an entry = that problem's CUE wrong rows plus its T3 wrong row); a resample with an empty denominator scores -inf (counted as refuted). Undefined statistic -> refuted_without_number. Pairs are pooled, so problems with 4 CUE wrong answers weigh 6 A pairs and 4 B pairs; math_verify timeouts inside grade could make a few agreements false.

predictions.experiment: Case where the effect should not appear: changing only the sampling rule under the same cue (T 1.0 / min-p 0.1) should keep the wrong values. Cross-file agreement C between day1_3 cued wrong answers and min-p cued wrong answers, minus within-file agreement A. A sampling-driven account (wrong values are per-draw accidents that any change of the sampler reshuffles) predicts C well below A.

CUE rows, CUE wrong answers, agreement (rln4_lib.agree from studies/rlneurons/lib/rln4_lib.py) and A exactly as in the first prediction (attempt == 0, first row per (problem_index, sample); wrong answer = cap_hit not true, finish_reason != 'length', score_v3 == 0, non-empty stripped extracted_v3; A = agreeing unordered same-problem pairs / all such pairs, pooled). MINP: keep rows with attempt == 0 or no attempt field, then the first row per problem_index in file order; a MINP row is a wrong answer under the same rule using its stored score_v3 and extracted_v3. C = (number of (CUE wrong answer, MINP wrong answer) pairs with the same problem_index that agree) / (number of such pairs), pooled. Statistic = C - A. If either denominator is 0 the statistic is undefined and counts as refuted.
predictions.refuted_by: measured C - A below -0.08, or undefined
predictions.note: Files: CUE as in k=1, and runs/theory-tests/frustea-1114-180849-456c/answers.jsonl (MINP; modal volume get iterate-runs frustea-1114-180849-456c/answers.jsonl; byte-identical to runs/theory-rows/frustea-1114-180849-456c/answers.jsonl named in the recipe). MINP uses its stored score_v3 and extracted_v3; rows kept if attempt is 0 or there is no attempt field, first row per problem_index. Statistic C - A, where C pairs CUE wrong answers with the MINP wrong answer of the same problem, agree(CUE, MINP), and A is as in k=1. Ambiguity: the order of agree's arguments; alt_measured uses agreement in either order. n = the smaller of the A group (problems with >= 2 CUE wrong) and the C group (problems with >= 1 CUE wrong and a MINP wrong). The refutation is measured < -0.08; undefined -> refuted_without_number. MINP has 1 sample per problem, so C rests on fewer problems than A.

predictions.experiment: Cause of the vote shortfall: among MATH-500 problems where the cued base has at least one right sample of 4 but the plurality vote is wrong, the share where the winning answer group has two or more members (agreeing wrong values), against singleton ties.
predictions.recipe: File: studies/rlneurons/results/day1_3/math500_base_cue-01/rows.jsonl. Keep rows with attempt == 0 and, for each (problem_index, sample) with sample in {0,1,2,3}, the first row in file order; keep problems that have all 4 samples. A sample is answer-bearing iff cap_hit is not true, finish_reason != 'length' and extracted_v3 is non-empty after strip(). A sample is right iff it is answer-bearing and score_v3 == 1. Grouping: process answer-bearing samples in increasing sample index; each joins the first existing group whose first member agrees with it under rln4_lib.agree (studies/rlneurons/lib/rln4_lib.py), else starts a new group. Winner = the group with the most members; ties go to the group whose first member has the lowest sample index. The vote is right iff the winner's first member has score_v3 == 1; with no answer-bearing sample the vote is wrong. F = problems with at least one right sample whose vote is wrong. Statistic = (problems in F whose winning group has 2 or more members) / |F|. If F is empty the statistic is undefined and counts as refuted.
predictions.note: File: CUE only (attempt 0, samples 0-3, first row per (problem_index, sample), problems with all 4 samples). Answer-bearing = cap_hit not true, finish_reason != 'length', non-empty stripped extracted_v3; right = answer-bearing and score_v3 == 1. Greedy grouping in sample order against each group's first member; winner = largest group, ties to the earliest-formed group (= lowest first-member sample index); vote right iff winner's first member has score_v3 == 1. F = problems with >= 1 right sample and a wrong vote; statistic = share of F whose winner has >= 2 members; n = |F|. Ambiguity: agree is asymmetric; main calls agree(first member, new sample); alt_measured uses agreement in either order (which can change both F and the numerator). Greedy grouping can split equivalent answers if the first member fails to parse; a right sample whose answer agrees with a wrong first member joins that wrong group. Bootstrap resamples all problems with 4 samples; an empty-F resample scores -inf.
